title: Xi'an's Great Mosque
hookLine: a mosque built like a Chinese temple, with a pagoda minaret

lines: A GATE WITH A CURVED TILED ROOF.
cards: Step off a crowded lane in the old city of Xi'an, past stalls selling dates and lamb skewers, through a gate with a curved tiled roof.
Inside: a garden courtyard, stone tablets carved with Chinese characters, a carved wooden archway, painted and lacquered. Then another courtyard, and another, each quieter than the last.
In the middle stands a tiered tower with upturned eaves like a pagoda. Everything says Chinese temple. Then, at the far end, people line up shoulder to shoulder, and someone calls Allahu akbar.

teach.h: BUILT IN THE LANGUAGE OF THE PLACE.
teach.b: Tradition says the Great Mosque of Xi'an goes back to the Tang dynasty; much of what stands today was built in later centuries. Either way, the builders made a choice.
They didn't import a domed mosque from somewhere else. They built in the language of the place: courtyards one after another, wooden halls on stone platforms, roofs of glazed tile.

teach.h: A PAGODA THAT SERVES AS A MINARET.
teach.b: The tower in the courtyard serves as the minaret, but it looks like a pagoda pavilion, and its Chinese name speaks of examining the heart.

teach.h: ARABIC AND CHINESE SIDE BY SIDE.
teach.b: In the prayer hall, Arabic verses and Chinese decoration sit side by side, sometimes so blended that the Arabic letters curl like Chinese brushwork. One thing doesn't change with the clothes.
The Qur'an tells the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship."

teach.h: ALL OF IT FACING WEST, TOWARD MECCA.
teach.b: In Xi'an that means west, toward Mecca, so the long line of courtyards runs east to west, and the prayer hall sits at the western end.
Chinese walls, Chinese roofs, a Chinese garden, and a direction that points across the continent to the Ka'ba.
Look back at this week: traders, not armies; the port of the straits; nine saints who taught with music; one faith in many island languages; the sultanates of the islands; the Hui.
This building holds the whole week in wood and tile. A mosque in Chinese dress.

how: The Great Mosque of Xi'an is still a working mosque for the Hui community of the city's old Muslim quarter, who pray there facing west toward Mecca; visitors walk through its courtyards outside prayer times.

games.why: they built in the language of the place, with courtyards and a pagoda tower, and turned the whole plan west toward Mecca.

practice: Walk slowly, in your mind, through the courtyards as they were described: the gate, the garden, the stone tablets, the tower, the long hall at the western end.
Notice which way you're walking, and look for one place where an Arabic word and a Chinese roof meet. If you pray, you can turn toward your own qibla.

wordCard.voice: Xi'an. The Chinese city whose Great Mosque is built like a Chinese temple, with a pagoda tower for a minaret and a prayer hall facing west. Today's word.
